title: Host staging slab and affinity steering to eliminate redundant memcpy and thread-lock storms
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Recent production traces show the host side of the prefill->decode pipeline accounting for a disproportionate fraction of tail latency and CPU usage. Root causes observed: multiple memcpy bounce copies between host buffers, repeated allocations/free of intermediate buffers, and threadpool lock contention when many short-lived requests arrive simultaneously. Goal: implement a low-overhead host staging layer (staged slab + pinned DMA pools) combined with lightweight affinity steering for worker threads to eliminate redundant copies and reduce lock storms without changing upstream APIs. This ticket drives the engineering work to prototype, benchmark, and land the staging + affinity changes and associated scheduler adjustments.
background: Metrics we observed in Feb 2026: host CPU per token for small chat prompts rose 2.7x at p95 during traffic spikes. End-to-end prefill tail (99th) shows 220ms variance attributable to host-side wait + memcpy. Existing host bridge uses ephemeral buffers and a central threadpool with a single mutex-protected queue; this pattern amplifies contention under bursty traffic. Prior mitigation attempts (tuning threadpool size) provided modest gains but didn't address duplicated copies when requests cross NUMA nodes.
approach: Introduce a page-aligned pinned buffer pool (pinned DMA slabs) per GPU device to avoid repeated allocation/pin/unpin cycles.
Add a lightweight staging slab allocator with size classes tuned for typical prefill/decode payloads to reuse host buffers and minimize fragmentation.
Implement a lock-free single-producer single-consumer (SPSC) ring for host->GPU handoff for steady single-request streams and a batched MPSC fallback for multi-producer bursts.
Add worker affinity steering: map incoming request shards to preferred host workers based on recent KV cache locality and NUMA node to reduce cross-node memcpy and remote memory accesses.
Fuse adjacent small memcpy operations into a single vectored/IOV memcpy where possible, and use asynchronous DMA when supported by the driver to overlap copies with kernel launches.
Expose a runtime flag to enable/disable pinned slabs and steering for quick rollback and A/B testing.
Run microbenchmarks and production A/B to validate gains, with clear rollback criteria in the rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Host-side per-request CPU (p50,p95) reduced by >=30% for small prompt workloads in controlled benchmark compared to baseline.
Total host->GPU memcpy bytes per minute reduced by >=45% in production A/B for the test cohort.
Tail latency (99th) for prefill->decode reduced by >=20ms on the test cohort and no regression on median latency.
Threadpool lock contention dropped (mutex hold counts down >=50%) as measured by perf events and custom tracing.
Feature gated, with runtime flag and telemetry to track adoption and potential regressions.
Docs updated: console/observability doc listing new metrics (staging_pool_hits, staging_pool_misses, memcpy_fused_bytes).

design_notes: We should keep slab allocations cache-friendly and power-of-two sized to make SPSC ring indices cheap.
NUMA: place pinned slabs local to the CPU socket paired with the GPU PCIe affinity; fall back to a shared pool only when exhausted.
Avoid exposing the slab pool to higher-level code; provide a thin lifecycle API (acquire/release) that is zero-copy for hot paths.
Steering policy must be conservative initially: prefer steering when pool hit rate > 70% and request size < 32KB to avoid adverse effects on large-batch workloads.
We will add counters for slab_hits, slab_misses, steering_applied, steering_failed to understand real-world behavior.

Safety: the staged buffer must be cleared before reuse to avoid information leakage across tenants; use explicit zeroing only for private deployments and overwrite for multi-tenant hosted deployments per policy.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: pinned pages increase memory pressure on hosts. Mitigation: implement soft cap and LRU draining under memory pressure signals.
Risk: steering can worsen performance for heterogeneous workloads. Mitigation: feature-gate steering and run canaries with diversified workload mixes.
Risk: driver async DMA path not available on all machines. Mitigation: detect capability at startup and fall back to synchronous fused memcpy path.
Risk: small leaks or stale data in reused buffers. Mitigation: add strict lifecycle and sanitizer checks in debug builds; require explicit test coverage.
